API and measurement lifecycle

Source: LIFECYCLE.md

Current distribution

The current stable release is 1.0.0. Pin the package version used in an analysis and run citation("ldfreq") to cite that exact release alongside the measurement methods and reference datasets used in your study.

The public development snapshot 1.0.0.9001 contains incompatible changes relative to 1.0.0, including changed raw-text defaults and retired entry points. It is not a stable 1.x release. See the migration instructions in the README and NEWS before using it. A future stable release containing incompatible changes requires a major version increment and migration notes.

Stability and reproducibility commitments

ldfreq treats lexical measures as auditable measurement specifications rather than opaque numbers:

  • Explicit method and parameter identities: Every metric row records its versioned method_id, requested and effective parameters, token and type counts (N, V), calculation status, and missing_reason.
  • Recorded preprocessing choices: Raw-text analyses (lexdiv_tokenize*(), lexdiv_metrics_text*()) default to case = "lower", tokenizer = "english", normalization = "NFC", and keep_numbers = FALSE, and record every setting and SHA-256 text fingerprint in $preprocessing.
  • Saved-result integrity: Exported corpus, annotation, and profile objects carry explicit S3 classes and integrity checks so accidental post-hoc edits cannot silently alter downstream tables or plots.
  • Deprecation policy: In the stable 1.x release series, public functions, argument names, and documented result columns are maintained compatibly; any future breaking change requires a major version increment and migration notes in NEWS.md.

Optional reference data

Third-party reference datasets are not bundled in the MIT-licensed package archive. Use lexdiv_resource_info() to inspect each dataset’s source, pinned version, SHA-256 digest, and license terms, then download selected resources explicitly with lexdiv_download_resources(..., accept_license = TRUE). Package installation and ordinary calculations never perform network requests.
